novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question (fixed-grid-certificate)
novelty_flags.one_line: Only Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin and Hauenstein--Sottile are positioned against the kernel; add Rump (2010) and a focused validated-global-optimization comparator, and explain why the resulting fixed three-node certificate rises above a subfield/letter case study to the required field tier.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question (fixed-grid-certificate) versus thm:finite-grid-existence and thm:pooled-wald
soundness_flags.one_line: The OEQ promises only the two witness Jacobian margins, whereas its stated dependencies define Gamma_T and kappa_T uniformly over every graph parameter box; either certify those uniform quantities or localize the downstream assumptions and theorems to the witness truth.

soundness_flags.label: ass:polynomial-poisson-mechanism; ass:coefficient-box; ass:fixed-exponents
soundness_flags.one_line: The fixed all-positive [1/2,3] edge box and one-linear/all-other-quadratic exponent map are instrumental separation assumptions with no assay calibration; the supplied justifications are witness-based and do not establish plausible gene-regulatory applicability, especially for inhibitory or weak edges.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:pooled-wald
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite-grid graph separation and the Jacobian margin are accepted as explicit conditional regularity premises for the Wald theorem, not as established conclusions.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Pointwise graph-selection and Wald coverage hold conditional on the stated positive separation, local identification, interiority, and variance premises; the OEQ must separately establish whichever of these it claims to operationalize.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: alphaCertified applies Smale alpha-theory to supplied square polynomial systems, certifying local approximate roots, distinct associated roots, and real roots; it does not globally exclude an analytic compact parameter domain.
The paper treats finite and continuum moment conditions and establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance-based optimal weighting under its regularity conditions.
The article is a published account of rigorous floating-point verification methods, directly relevant to the interval Newton/Krawczyk and branch-and-bound portion of the proposed certificate handle.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the one-instance certificate OEQ with a finite-input certified decision procedure for (M,T,coefficient boxes,w_max,N_max), specifying outputs, termination conditions, and an arithmetic or subdivision-complexity bound; this creates a reusable constructive-identifiability contribution.

Make the certificate and inference layers agree: either certify Gamma_T and kappa_T uniformly over the declared boxes, or redefine the GMM assumptions and Wald theorem around a local true-parameter margin that the fixed witness certificate actually proves.

Add validated-numerics prior art, especially Rump (2010), and state the precise new ingredient beyond generic interval verification: analytic PGF tail enclosure jointly propagated through graph exclusion, singular-value certification, and causal-contrast precision.

Calibrate the polynomial exponent and edge-size restrictions using a concrete sorted-cell assay or retarget the paper explicitly as a synthetic protocol; allow an evidence-backed treatment of weak and inhibitory effects if prospective biological relevance remains the stated consumer.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: promote the fixed numerical exercise into a reusable certified decision-procedure theorem, reconcile local versus uniform margins, and substantiate the restrictive biological subclass before returning for field-tier review.
